Spanish.description: Spoken across Spain and the Americas. Characterized by transparent phonetics and rich verbal morphology.

French.description: Global language of diplomacy and literature, featuring nasal vowels, liaison, and deep lexical ties to English.

German.description: Europe's most widely spoken native tongue in the EU, renowned for expressive compound nouns and three grammatical genders.

Italian.description: The closest national descendant of Latin in vocabulary, celebrated for melodic vowel endings and musical terminology.

Portuguese.description: Transcontinental language of Brazil, Portugal, and Lusophone Africa with distinctive nasal diphthongs and rhythmic cadence.
